plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Exit all holdings flagged for sale by the scanner (METU, MUU, SMCI).
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Increase exposure to SPY to 25% for broad market stability and quality.
This plan aims for capital preservation and reduced overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return potential, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and high-beta single names. Expect lower volatility and more stable, albeit slower, growth.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to small, manageable positions.
Reduce exposure to METU and MUU, and sell SMCI, all flagged by the scanner.
Trim QQQI to 20% to comply with the single-name concentration mandate.
Introduce new positions in TXN and AAPU, both strong scanner setups, for growth.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5%/month growth, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding quality tech names. Expect moderate volatility and a blend of broad market stability with targeted growth opportunities.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to lean into market momentum.
Add to METU and MUU, despite scanner flags, for aggressive sector concentration.
Sell SMCI as it is a flagged sell and below its stop.
Trim QQQI to 15% to free up capital for higher-growth opportunities.
Buy TXN and AAPU at 6% each, leveraging strong scanner setups for aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month growth, stretching for higher returns. It significantly increases leverage and concentration, leading to higher potential upside but also substantially greater drawdown risk. Daily decay and rebalancing of leveraged ETFs can erode capital quickly; strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions and low drawdown. It significantly reduces exposure to high-beta and leveraged assets. While aiming for consistent income, remember distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
